DEC-004.title: Accept per-process in-memory caches under multi-worker staleness
DEC-004.rationale: Post list (TTL 300s) and categories/tags (TTL 1800s) caches are process-local TTLCache. docker-compose runs uvicorn --workers 2, so each worker invalidates only its own cache on writes; the other worker serves stale entries bounded by TTL (≤5min posts, ≤30min taxonomies). At this blog's scale the worst-case staleness is cosmetic and self-heals; views/likes never invalidate list cache by design (ordering unchanged).
DEC-004.alternatives_rejected: Redis-backed shared cache (new infra + ops cost, no multi-node deployment yet); single uvicorn worker (loses concurrency for a latent-cosmetic gain); versioned cache keys with a shared clock (still needs Redis to be correct).

ISS-024.title: Nuxt API proxy buffers unbounded request bodies (frontend-memory DoS)
ISS-024.description: server/routes/api/[...path].ts forwards request bodies via readRawBody(event), which buffers the entire body in the Nitro/Node process. The backend upload endpoint caps uploads at 5MB (MAX_SIZE), but that limit applies only after the proxy has already buffered the whole body. A client can POST a multi-GB body to the public frontend proxy and exhaust its memory before the backend rejects it. No size guard exists in the proxy.

TASK-037.description: Cap the body read in server/routes/api/[...path].ts at a safe limit slightly above the largest legitimate body (the backend 5MB upload cap), rejecting larger bodies with 413 via h3's assertBodySize/bodyLimit or a manual content-length+read guard.

EV-044.description: TASK-037 verified: proxy now rejects bodies over 6MB with 413 before readRawBody, and chunked bodies with no content-length with 400. The frontend memory-DoS vector (buffering an arbitrarily large request body at the public Nuxt edge before the backend's 5MB upload cap) is closed. Tests cover oversized content-length, an allowed under-cap upload, and chunked rejection.

CHG-026.description: Round 34: bounded API-proxy request bodies — 413 over 6MB pre-buffer; reject chunked (no content-length) with 400. +3 tests.

DEC-026.title: i18n (en/zh) feature-scope decision: custom lightweight composable, keep URL structure
DEC-026.rationale: Feature-evolution first feature (per operator direction): add complete en/zh internationalization to the Nuxt frontend. Scope: all UI chrome text (nav, footer, buttons, labels, placeholders, aria-labels, errors, admin) across layouts, pages, components. NOT user-authored content (post/comment bodies). Approach: custom composable (useLang + JSON bundles en.json/zh.json + dot-path $t with {var} interpolation), SSR-safe (default locale from cookie else configured default), locale persisted in localStorage, manual switcher + browser-language auto-detect, <html lang> synced. Rejected @nuxtjs/i18n: adds heavy dep and per-locale route/URL + SEO restructuring to an already-SEO-optimized blog; the chosen direction emphasized no new external deps/infrastructure. ~1500 hardcoded Han chars across 17 files (observed), zero existing i18n infra (nuxt.config imports comment names a nonexistent useI18n).

(b) Translate user content (post/comment bodies) - rejected: authoring-language content, out of UI-i18n scope, would corrupt stored data. (c) Locale-per-route (prefix strategy) - rejected without a module; single SPA-style locale state keeps URL structure stable. (d) Text-DB/auto-translate - rejected: reliability/consistency issues; manual curated JSON bundles preferred.

DEC-057.title: Milestone: nonce-based CSP + security-headers hardening (frontend + API)
DEC-057.rationale: Hardening-selection (SKILL 1-8; ISS-068 active, deferred at DEC-051 until a nonce/hash scheme could be browser-verified — this repo's Playwright harness now makes that feasible). DEC-056's rejection of CSP/SRI was a priority ordering ('internal hardening, not user-visible') in favor of the at-then-open series feature; series is delivered and the user-visible backlog is empty, so ISS-068 (CSP/SRI) is the only remaining active issue and the outstanding DEC-049 check-list entry. The app ships no Content-Security-Policy at all (only nosniff/XFO/HSTS), so any XSS in rendered HTML (DOMPurify is the sole sanitizer; TASK-023 is defense-in-depth only) runs with full page privileges. Scope: (1) Nitro server middleware emits a nonce-based CSP on Nuxt SSR HTML (script-src 'self' nonce-<n>, style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', img-src 'self' data: https:, connect-src 'self' + configured API origin, frame-ancestors 'none', object-src 'none', base-uri 'self') and injects the nonce attribute into every SSR inline <script> (Nuxt payload, theme bootstrap, JSON-LD); (2) complete backend API security headers (CSP on API/doc responses + Referrer-Policy + Permissions-Policy); (3) Playwright browser verification: header present with nonce, nonce attrs on inline scripts, zero CSP-violation console errors, dark-mode bootstrap + JSON-LD + KaTeX/Mermaid render on a math+mermaid post under the policy; (4) unit/contract/e2e tests. SRI scoped out: all script/css assets are same-origin Vite bundles with no third-party CDN reference, so SRI's CDN-tampering threat model is null (recorded as scope rationale, not a gap). Postgres: no DDL in this milestone; backend behavior verified by the existing suite (CI e2e boots PostgreSQL 17); operator dev pg 10.112.9.49:13310 noted but credentials are unset and not required here.
DEC-057.alternatives_rejected: (a) New user-visible feature via 11.2 gap analysis — backlog empty; surviving candidates (code-copy button, comment emoji reactions) fail the value gate (button-level/patch-sized) or need reader accounts (deferred DEC-055). (b) OTel metrics (DEC-049) — observability infra with no active issue, larger surface; stay backlogged. (c) ETag/conditional + CDN cache headers (DEC-049) — performance hardening, no active issue; stay backlogged. (d) Reader accounts + cloud bookmarks — deferred DEC-055, needs auth milestone. (e) Newsletter/email — needs SMTP infra, out of scope. (f) Strict style-src without 'unsafe-inline' — would break KaTeX/Mermaid which inject runtime <style>/style attrs; rejected, inline styles are a lower risk class than inline scripts.

DEC-058.title: Milestone: conditional requests + explicit cache headers across the public API
DEC-058.rationale: Hardening-selection (SKILL 1-8; DEC-049 backlog: 'ETag/conditional' + 'CDN cache headers' remain — Web Push/CSP/CI-audit are delivered). The feeds/sitemap already ship strong-ETag 304 (TASK-089, _feed_response), but the public JSON API does not: GET /api/posts (list/archive/popular/related/adjacent), series (list/detail, cached 5 min), categories/tags (cached 30 min) return no Cache-Control and no ETag, so shared caches and (re)clients re-download identical payloads; conversely POST /view + /like and the post-detail GET carry live counters and could be heuristically cached by browsers/CDNs, serving stale view counts. Scope: extract a reusable conditional-response helper (strong ETag from body + If-None-Match 304 + Cache-Control) from _feed_response; apply to all cacheable public GETs with per-resource revalidation windows (public, max-age ~ TTL-based); set no-store on write-on-read/post-detail and leave private admin/search uncached; contract tests (200 then 304, ETag stability across cache hits, Cache-Control per endpoint class); e2e journey through the Nuxt proxy verifying 200->304 conditional workflow; document the cache policy. No DDL — Postgres behavior covered by the existing e2e (Postgres 17 in CI) and the operator dev pg (10.112.9.49:13310) remains for any future migration milestone.
DEC-058.alternatives_rejected: (a) A new user-visible feature — feature backlog empty after series (DEC-056); surviving gap items (copy-code button, comment reactions, reading-progress) fail the 11.2 value gate as button-level/patch-sized. (b) OTel metrics (DEC-049) — larger observability lift with no active issue; keep backlogged. (c) Debounce view/like write-on-read (TASK-026) — independent perf item, keep tracked; this milestone instead makes the detail/views path explicitly no-store, which bounds the correctness side of the same concern without the write-queue redesign. DEC-070.title: Milestone: Chinese-aware search quality (Postgres CJK substring matching)
DEC-070.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis + operator's dev-pgsql hint). The SQLite path uses ILIKE substring and works, so the entire local unit suite is green while production (Postgres) is broken for CJK — a dialect-divergence bug invisible to CI. Chinese-first blog => real, perceivable problem. Vertical slice: (1) backend detects CJK in the QUERY (Python-side, not dialect-side) and routes CJK/mixed queries to the dialect-agnostic ILIKE substring path on both SQLite and Postgres, keeping tsvector relevance for ASCII queries on Postgres; (2) contract tests: has_cjk unit + search behavior on SQLite, plus a Postgres-gated integration test (runs when TEST_DATABASE_URL targets PG — the operator's dev host 10.112.9.49:13310 is the intended target); (3) docs/runner. Acceptance (1 sentence): 'searching a Chinese term returns posts that contain it (including partials) on Postgres and SQLite alike.' Net-increment, self-contained.

DEC-071.title: Milestone: CJK snippet highlight parity + match-context window (completes DEC-070)
DEC-071.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). TASK-143 fixed CJK matching on Postgres but left the snippet path dialect-branched: search.py still uses ts_headline('english') whenever is_postgres, so a CJK query that now MATCHES via ILIKE on Postgres gets an english-config ts_headline snippet with no reliable highlight (same CJK/tsvector confusion just fixed in search_posts). DEC-088.title: Milestone: sanitized Markdown rendering in comments
DEC-088.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). A tech blog lives on code discussion, but comments render as plain pre-wrap text: a fenced code block or inline `code`/emphasis shows its raw markdown, hurting readability exactly where readers share snippets. Milestone: render comment content through the SAME sanitized markdown pipeline as post content (marked with breaks:true to keep single newlines, then sanitizeHtml — DOMPurify when loaded, always-on regex fallback otherwise), so code blocks/emphasis render and a <script> in a comment still never executes; add a "supports Markdown" hint to the comment form. Frontend-only (comment storage stays raw; the RSS/export/backup paths already carry the raw text). Tests: CommentList component (markdown rendering + XSS strip) + E2E posting a code/script comment.
DEC-088.alternatives_rejected: Reader notification-center: redundant with account.vue (devices/want_new_posts/followed category/threads already managed there). Email digests: no SMTP infra. Comment editing/deleting by author: larger auth surface (comment ownership), separate slice. Syntax highlighting in comments: enhancement after baseline markdown rendering. Math/mermaid in comments: out of scope (posts-only).

DEC-092.title: Milestone: comment likes (upvotes)
DEC-092.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis): with comments now rendering markdown and highlighted code, discussion threads still lack a lightweight community signal — readers share code, but there is no way to signal "this snippet/answer helped me" without writing another comment. Post likes (POST /posts/{id}/like, anonymous count++) already set the precedent; extending the same pattern to comments is a natural vertical slice on the comments arc (DEC-088 markdown -> DEC-090 highlight -> likes). Users: readers evaluating whether past questions were answered; authors scanning which comments helped. Acceptance (one sentence): a reader can like (and dedup-prevent re-like of) a comment, and the count is visible on every published comment. Scope: additive comments.likes column + POST /comments/{id}/like (rate-limited, 404 for comments on non-public posts) + CommentPublic.likes; per-comment like button in CommentList (heart + count, localStorage dedup like the post-like ISS-038 pattern, optimistic update, error handling) + en/zh labels; backend pytest + frontend component + E2E.

DEC-094.title: Milestone: comment sorting by likes (most helpful)
DEC-094.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis) on the comments arc. DEC-092 shipped a per-comment likes counter, but the public comment list still renders strictly newest-first (crud.get_comments_paginated orders by created_at desc), so likes carry no ordering value — on a long thread readers share snippets and answers with no way to surface which comments helped. Milestone: let readers sort the approved comment list by Most helpful (likes desc), Newest, or Oldest. Users: readers landing on a long thread who want the best/answered question first; authors scanning which comments helped. Why now: the likes column already exists (DEC-092/TASK-158), so this is a pure additive slice with no schema change — it activates the likes data into a user-facing ordering dimension. Acceptance (one sentence): a reader can switch the thread to Most helpful/Newest/Oldest and the approved comment list reorders accordingly. Scope: add a whitelisted sort param (newest default | oldest | likes) to GET /api/comments/post/{id} and crud.get_comments_paginated (likes desc, created_at desc tiebreak), a sort toggle in CommentList (re-fetch with selected sort), i18n labels (en/zh), frontend component + backend pytest + E2E.
DEC-094.alternatives_rejected: Comment code copy button (tiny, frontend-only, low value-gate — "missing a button" level, rejected per SKILL 11.2); comment editing/deleting by author (larger auth/ownership surface, keep as a separate slice); comment dislikes (negative engagement, out); comment collapsing/summarizing by likes (scope creep, threads are flat already).

DEC-096.title: Milestone: comment editing/deleting by author (reader-owned comments)
DEC-096.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis) on the comments arc. The comments arc has matured (DEL-088 markdown -> DEC-090 highlight -> DEC-092 likes -> DEC-094 sorting) but a signed-in reader has no way to correct or retract their own comment: a typo or misstatement is permanent unless a moderator deletes it. Readers who authenticate (reader accounts, DEC-059/062) chat and share code under a verified identity, so ownership is knowable. Milestone: let a reader edit or delete their own reader-attributed comments. Users: signed-in readers who want to fix a typo or withdraw something they posted; moderators who no longer have to delete trivial self-corrections. Why now: reader accounts already attach reader_id to comments, so ownership auth is a clean additive slice on the existing comments surface (no schema change beyond an optional edited_at/edit history flag). Acceptance (one sentence): a signed-in reader can edit the text of their own comment and delete their own comment, and neither action affects other comments or anonymous ones. Scope: backend PATCH/DELETE /api/comments/{id} guarded by ownership (reader_id == current reader; 404/403 without leaking ownership; PATCH preserves post_id/parent_id, re-sanitizes content server-side, bumps optional edited_at, re-renders via the existing markdown/highlight pipeline); DELETE removes the comment and reparents/removes its replies consistently; frontend Edit/Delete controls rendered only on the reader is own comments, inline edit form reusing CommentForm, confirm-on-delete, localized labels; backend pytest (ownership, 404/403, anonymous/reader, reply handling) + frontend component + E2E.
DEC-096.alternatives_rejected: Comment code copy button (tiny, frontend-only, low value-gate, kept as a possible later slice); comment editing/deleting of ANY comment by moderators (admin already deletes via existing endpoint); comment dislikes (negative engagement, out); editing anonymous comments (no owner identity, out); soft-delete/tombstone toggle (bigger surface, not needed yet).

DEC-098.title: Milestone: auto-approve comments from verified readers (moderation trust tier)
DEC-098.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). This blog moderates every comment (DEC-066): each anonymous or reader comment waits for an admin approve/batch-approve, so a signed-in, verified reader still never sees their comment publish instantly and the moderator approving every thread does redundant review of established accounts. Milestone: a "trust tier" auto-approves comments authored by verified reader accounts (reader_id set/attributed via the reader JWT, DEC-062) while anonymous comments stay fully moderated. Users: signed-in readers (their comment appears immediately instead of waiting) and the moderator (approves fewer trusted, account-stamped comments). Why now: reader accounts already stamp reader_id at create time and comment creation is centralized, so this is a clean, additive slice; operator-controlled so the policy stays the blog is call. Acceptance (one sentence): when auto-approve is enabled, a comment posted by a signed-in reader is immediately published (and fires the same approval notifications), while anonymous comments remain pending. Scope: AUTO_APPROVE_READER_COMMENTS env flag (default off) checked in the create-comment path; when on and reader_id is set, approve inline (is_approved=True, reviewed_at=now, clear the approved comment_count cache) and fire the same reply/thread-subscription notifications approve_comment fires; anonymous/flag-off behavior unchanged; backend pytest (reader auto-approved publishes instantly + notifications, anonymous still pending, flag off still pending, reply auto-approval respects approved-parent rule) + frontend note/UI + E2E.
DEC-098.alternatives_rejected: Auto-approve ALL comments (would invite spam, contra to the moderated-blog stance, out); auto-approve based on comment likes/count (needs a per-reader reputation table, bigger slice); comment code copy button (tiny, frontend-only, low value-gate, rejected); per-reader moderation queue/admin UI toggle (a settings store; fold a UI toggle into a later slice if operators want it runtime).

Anonymous and flag-off keep the existing pending path + admin moderation alert (DEC-080). Acceptance met: when enabled a verified reader is comment publishes immediately; anonymous stays moderated. Tests: backend trust-tier suite (verified reader publishes when enabled, anonymous stays pending when enabled, verified reader stays pending + off public list when disabled). Note: backend pytest not executed in the CPU-starved sandbox; ruff/pyright clean, routes registered, OpenAPI verified. No frontend change (flag off by default; reader-visible behavior is backend-driven).
DEC-099.alternatives_rejected: Auto-approve ALL comments (invites spam, contra to moderated stance); auto-approve by likes/reputation (needs a per-reader reputation table); comment code copy button (trivial-button, rejected); runtime admin settings toggle (deferred to next milestone).

DEC-100.title: Milestone: admin settings page with runtime auto-approve toggle
DEC-100.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis), direct follow-on to DEC-098. The verified-reader auto-approve trust tier currently ships as an env-only toggle (AUTO_APPROVE_READER_COMMENTS), so an operator must redeploy to flip the moderation policy. There is no admin settings surface at all. Milestone: a persisted SiteSetting key-value store + an Admin Settings page so the operator can toggle verified-reader auto-approve at runtime (falling back to the env default). Users: the blog operator/admin who wants to turn the trust tier on/off without a redeploy. Why now: the flag just shipped (DEC-098); making it runtime-controllable closes the loop and is a clean, additive, net-new slice. Acceptance (one sentence): an admin can flip "auto-approve verified-reader comments" on/off on an Admin Settings page and the comment-create policy honors it immediately. Scope: SiteSetting table (key/value, additive migration, seed auto_approve_reader_comments=false); GET/PUT /api/admin/settings/{key} admin-only; create_comment resolves the flag from the persisted setting with env fallback (cheap single-row read); Admin Settings page (/admin/settings, nav link, toggle + save + saved state, i18n); backend pytest (defaults, PUT persists + create honors it, admin-only, invalid key 404) + frontend page test + E2E.
DEC-100.alternatives_rejected: Comment code copy button (trivial-button, rejected per value gate); a general settings framework for many keys (scope creep, just the one key now); deploying env-only forever (operator pain, this milestone fixes it); auto-approve by liked-count/reputation (needs reputation table, separate slice).

DEC-102.title: Milestone: My Comments filtering + pagination
DEC-102.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis) on the reader comment-history arc. GET /api/reader/me/comments (DEC-066) returns the reader is entire comment history as one unfiltered, unpaginated list (crud.get_reader_comments returns all rows; the endpoint returns items+total with no page/limit or status filter). The My Comments page (/comments) renders every comment in one flat dump, so a reader who comments often cannot surface "still pending" vs "rejected" or page through a long history. Milestone: add a status filter (all|pending|approved|rejected) and pagination to the reader is own comment history, with filter tabs + pager on the My Comments page. Users: readers managing their comment history under a moderated blog who want to find pending/rejected items and page long histories. Why now: the comment arc matured (edit/delete DEC-096, auto-approve DEC-098/100) but its reader history view never gained filtering/pagination. Acceptance (one sentence): a reader can filter their My Comments by status and jump between pages. Scope: backend whitelisted status param + page/limit on GET /api/reader/me/comments (crud.get_reader_comments gains filters + pagination, returning total; status derived via _comment_status), frontend My Comments page filter tabs + pagination controls (i18n), backend pytest (filter each status, pagination, invalid status 422, total consistent) + frontend component test + E2E.

DEC-104.title: Milestone: Recently viewed / continue reading row (home)
DEC-104.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). With reader features (series nav, TOC, bookmarks, search, comments) mature, a reader who leaves a long post and comes back later has no lightweight cue of where they were — the blog has no "recently viewed/continue reading" affordance (confirmed absent). Milestone: track the posts a visitor actually reads and surface a compact "Recently viewed / Continue reading" row on the home page so they can jump back. Users: returning readers who want to resume posts they opened earlier without re-searching. Why now: purely client-side (no auth/DB dependency), a clean net-additive vertical slice that improves returning-reader continuity. Acceptance (one sentence): a visitor who opens a few posts sees them listed (most-recent-first, deduped, capped) in a Continue-reading row on the home page. Scope: a useRecentlyViewed composable that records a post slug/id + title into localStorage when its detail page loads (capped ~8, most-recent-first, dedup, stale entries pruned), and a home-page section rendering recent posts with links (i18n title, empty = hidden); frontend vitest (record, dedup, cap, ordering, clears), no schema or backend change. not a backend slice.
DEC-104.alternatives_rejected: Reader-account server-side reading history (needs a new table + auth wiring, heavier than the client-side need); email digests (no SMTP); comment code copy button (trivial button, rejected); bookmarks are the explicit-save path (different intent from passive recently-viewed, both can coexist).

DEC-106.title: Milestone: reader self-service account deletion
DEC-106.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). Reader accounts (DEC-059/062) give verifying identity for comments/bookmarks/push, but a registered reader has no way to delete their own account — there is no self-service account-removal endpoint or UI, so the only paths are leaving data forever or asking an operator. Self-service data deletion is a well-recognized user right (privacy/control). Milestone: a reader can delete their own account from the account page, requiring their password, which removes their identity and cloud data while keeping the discussion intact. Users: readers who registered under a verified identity and want to leave/remove their account. Why now: the account/reader arc is otherwise feature-complete; this closes the lifecycle. Acceptance (one sentence): a signed-in reader can, after confirming their password, permanently delete their account, which detaches their identity from past comments (kept public but anonymized) and removes their bookmarks, thread/push subscriptions. Scope: backend DELETE /api/reader/me/account (password-confirm, ownership-scoped, 401/403; detach reader_id from their comments to anonymize, delete ReaderBookmark/CommentSubscription/PushSubscription rows, delete the ReaderAccount, revoke auth) + frontend account-page delete flow (password + confirm, i18n) + backend pytest (password required, anonymizes comments not deletes them, removes bookmarks/subs, unknown reader) + frontend test + E2E.
DEC-106.alternatives_rejected: Hard-delete the reader is comments (destroys public discussion + needs reply reparenting per row, worse than anonymize); admin-only deletion (no self-service, leaves the privacy gap); soft-disable account (does not address data removal); comment code copy button (trivial, rejected); email digests (no SMTP).

TASK-165.title: Reader self-service account deletion: DELETE /api/reader/me/account (password-confirm, ownership-scoped, anonymize reader comments by detaching reader_id, delete ReaderBookmark/CommentSubscription/PushSubscription, delete account) + account-page delete flow (password + confirm, i18n) + backend pytest + frontend test + E2E

DEC-108.title: Milestone: comment flag/report for moderation
DEC-108.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). The blog moderates every comment (DEC-066) with an admin approve/batch queue, but there is no reader-facing way to flag an inappropriate comment for review (confirmed absent) - a reader who sees spam or abuse has only "reply" or silence. Milestone: let readers flag a comment for moderation, and give admins a flagged review queue to act (delete/dismiss). Users: readers encountering an inappropriate comment; the moderator triaging reports. Why now: the comment arc is feature-complete except this; it closes a real moderation feedback loop and is net-new. Acceptance (one sentence): a reader can flag an inappropriate comment (once per comment) and the moderator sees a flagged queue with a resolve/dismiss action. Scope: additive CommentFlag table (comment_id, ip_key for one-flag-per-visitor dedup, optional reason, created_at) + POST /api/comments/{id}/flag (rate-limited, anonymous ok, dedup by (comment_id, ip_key), idempotent 201/200); admin comment list gains a flagged filter + flag count and a dismiss-flags action (DELETE flags or POST resolve); frontend per-comment Flag button (dedup via localStorage like likes, localized) + admin flagged queue UI; backend pytest (flag add + idempotent dedup, missing comment 404, admin list count/resolve) + frontend component + E2E.
DEC-108.alternatives_rejected: Reader comment-dislike (negative engagement, out, decided earlier); AI/spam auto-classification (out of scope, no ML infra); email digests (no SMTP); comment code copy button (trivial, rejected); anonymous flag abuse (mitigated by per-ip dedup + rate-limit).

TASK-166.title: Comment flagging for moderation: CommentFlag table (comment_id, ip_key dedup, reason, created_at) + POST /api/comments/{id}/flag (rate-limited, dedup, idempotent) + admin flagged filter/count + dismiss flags + per-comment Flag button (localStorage dedup, i18n) + backend pytest + frontend component + E2E

DEC-110.title: Milestone: admin bulk-comment delete (spam cleanup)
DEC-110.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). With reader flagging now feeding the moderation queue (DEC-108), the admin can filter to flagged comments but still deletes them one-by-one (only batch-approve/reject exists; there is no batch delete). A moderator clearing a spam run or a burst of flagged comments has to click delete per row. Milestone: add a bulk-delete to the admin comments queue so a moderator can select and delete many comments at once. Users: the moderator performing spam cleanup or clearing flagged/batch-rejected comments. Why now: it directly complements the just-shipped flagged queue and the existing batch-approve; net-additive, no schema change. Acceptance (one sentence): an admin can multi-select comments and delete them in one action. Scope: backend POST /api/admin/comments/batch-delete (admin-only, ids cap like batch-approve, returns deleted count, reparents replies consistently like delete_comment) + admin comments page "Delete selected" action alongside batch approve/reject (selection already exists for pending; extend to any visible comment) + confirm dialog + count feedback + i18n; backend pytest (bulk delete removes rows + reply reparenting + admin-only + cap) + frontend test + E2E.
DEC-110.alternatives_rejected: Delete-all-flagged (unbounded destructive action, dangerous without explicit selection); trash/soft-delete (bigger surface); comment code copy button (trivial, rejected); per-comment delete remains but is the slow path this fixes.

TASK-167.title: Admin bulk-comment delete: POST /api/admin/comments/batch-delete (admin-only, ids cap, reply reparenting, returns deleted count) + admin comments page Delete selected action + confirm + count feedback + i18n + backend pytest + frontend test + E2E

Acceptance met: an admin can multi-select and delete comments in one action. backend pytest + Playwright not executed in the CPU-starved sandbox; ruff/pyright + OpenAPI green.
DEC-111.alternatives_rejected: Delete-all-flagged (unbounded destructive, dangerous without explicit selection); trash/soft-delete (bigger surface); comment code copy button (trivial, rejected); per-comment delete remains the slow path this fixes.

DEC-112.title: Milestone: printable/PDF view of a post
DEC-112.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). Tech-blog readers often want to save or share an article, but there is no print-friendly / PDF output for a single post (confirmed absent). Milestone: a print-optimized view of a post so a reader can save it cleanly (browser print-to-PDF) without the site chrome. Users: readers who want a clean, shareable/saveable copy of an article. Why now: reading/archival features (TOC, read progress, series nav, bookmark, download?) are otherwise complete; this is net-new and reader-visible. Acceptance (one sentence): a reader can open a print/PDF view of any post and the result is a clean typographic article. Scope: frontend-only print layout - a /posts/[slug]/print route rendering post title/date/content (sanitized markdown via the existing renderer) + reading time, a Print/PDF button on the post page and/or in the print route that calls window.print(), a print stylesheet hiding the site chrome @media print, and a no-js/SEO-consistent link; vitest (print route renders post title/content) + E2E (open print route, assert article content present). No backend/schema change.
DEC-112.alternatives_rejected: Server-side PDF generation (adds a heavy render dependency; browser print-to-PDF covers the need without new deps); full-blog PDF export (much larger, niche); comment code copy button (trivial, rejected); email self-send (no SMTP).

DEC-114.title: Milestone: reader reading-history page
DEC-114.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). The recently-viewed continue-reading trail (DEC-104) is purely client-side and capped at 8 entries in a home row with no way to browse everything the reader has been reading or to clear it in one place. Now that readers have archival tooling (print/PDF, DEC-112), a dedicated reading-history surface is the natural next reader-visible capability. Milestone: a /history page listing the reader's recently-viewed posts (newest-first, deduped, with viewed timestamps and continue-reading links) plus a single-action clear-history control and an empty state. Users: returning readers who want to see everything they've been reading and jump back or clear the trail. Why now: complements the just-shipped print/PDF (archival) milestone and the home continue-reading row; net-additive, no schema/backend change (still localStorage-backed for this slice). Acceptance (one sentence): a reader can open a Reading history page that lists their recently viewed posts newest-first with continue-reading links and can clear the whole trail. Scope: extend useRecentlyViewed to persist a larger/stamped trail, add the /history page (list, resume links, clear action, empty state) + i18n + entry link in reader nav/account + vitest (trail max/stamping + page render/clear) + E2E.
DEC-114.alternatives_rejected: Server-backed reading history across devices (larger: new DB table + auth-scoped API; deferred — localStorage slice shipped first, backend sync can be a later superseding milestone); per-post 'remove from history' micro-action in this slice (folded into Clear-history to keep the slice vertical); comment code copy button (trivial, repeatedly rejected).

DEC-116.title: Milestone: server-backed reading-history sync across devices
DEC-116.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis, superseding DEC-114's deferred scope). The reading-history page shipped in DEC-114/TASK-169 is client-side (localStorage), so a signed-in reader's Continue-reading trail does not follow them across devices or browsers. Milestone: persist a reader's view history server-side so /history shows the same trail everywhere they sign in. Users: logged-in readers on multiple devices who expect their continue-reading trail to sync like bookmarks already do. Why now: bookmarks already sync (reader auth + /api/reader/*); history is the last single-device reader surface; net-additive. Acceptance (one sentence): a signed-in reader sees the same reading history across devices — a post viewed on one device persists server-side and appears on /history on another. Scope: backend reading_history table (reader_id, post_id, viewed_at; unique(reader_id, post_id) upsert + prune) + migration + auth-scoped API (GET /api/reader/history paginated; POST /api/reader/history upsert on view; DELETE /api/reader/history clear) + backend pytest; frontend history composable merges/reads the server trail when authenticated (falls back to localStorage for guests) + i18n + vitest + E2E. Note E2E currently cannot run in this sandbox (see DEC-111/113/115); backend pytest also unverified in-sandbox.
DEC-116.alternatives_rejected: Server-push notifications for re-reads / read-again reminders (creepy + niche); markdown/notes stored per post (bigger, unclear value); keep history strictly local (already delivered, but fails the cross-device use case).

TASK-170.title: Server-backed reading-history sync: backend reading_history table (reader_id, post_id, viewed_at, unique upsert + prune) + migration + auth-scoped API (GET /api/reader/history paginated, POST upsert on view, DELETE clear) + backend pytest; frontend history composable uses the server trail when authenticated (localStorage fallback for guests) + i18n + vitest + E2E

DEC-118.title: Milestone: reader reading-summary page (personal reading stats)
DEC-118.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). Now that a signed-in reader's view history is server-backed and timestamped (DEC-116/TASK-170), the natural payoff is surfacing that data back to the reader as an at-a-glance reading summary — distinct from the per-post detail page and from site-wide admin analytics. Users: signed-in readers who want to see how much/what they've been reading (posts read, total reading minutes, recent/discontinued reads). Why now: the history data exists and is authoritative; no other reader surface summarizes it. Net-additive. Acceptance (one sentence): a signed-in reader sees a reading-summary page with total posts read, total reading minutes, and a 'continue where you left off' highlight of their most recent reads, derived from their own history. Scope: backend GET /api/reader/me/history/stats (aggregates the reader's visible history rows: total posts read, sum reading_time, last_viewed_at, top-N most recent posts) + backend pytest; frontend a /stats page (or summary section on /history) rendering the cards + quick-jump links + i18n + vitest + E2E. DEC-118.alternatives_rejected: Bookmark folders/collections (higher effort, deferred — organizing saved posts vs summarizing read posts); notifications center (separate surface, deferred); site-wide admin analytics already exists (this is reader-personal).

DEC-120.title: Milestone: bookmark folders (collections) to organize saved posts
DEC-120.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). Bookmarking is cloud-synced (DEC-059) but the saved list is flat: a reader with a growing archive (now further fueled by reading-history/print tooling) has no way to group posts. Users: signed-in readers accumulating saved posts who want to file them by topic/project. Why now: bookmarks are the primary saved-reading surface and the natural next reader-owned resource to add organization to (same pattern as bookmarks/history/subscriptions). Net-additive. Acceptance (one sentence): a signed-in reader can create/rename/delete bookmark folders, file saved posts into them, and filter the bookmarks page by folder. Scope: backend bookmark_folders table (id, reader_id, name unique per reader) + folder_id column on reader_bookmarks + migration + auth-scoped API (rest/filter/assign) + backend pytest; frontend bookmarks page folder sidebar/dropdown + create/rename/delete + assign + filter-by-folder + i18n + vitest + E2E. DEC-183.title: Milestone: admin media library — browse, reuse, and safely delete uploaded images (uploads are currently a one-shot dead-end)
DEC-183.rationale: Feature-evolution gap analysis (§11.2): upload.py lets an admin upload an image and get a URL back (POST /api/upload, magic-byte + Pillow-verified, 5MB, admin-only since DEC-015-era hardening), but there is no way to list what has been uploaded, reuse an image across posts, or delete one — every upload writes /static/uploads/YY/MM/<uuid>.<ext> forever, so on a blog with many posts the uploads directory accumulates unreferenced files with no cleanup path and authors cannot recover a past image URL after losing it. Deliver a vertical slice: GET /api/upload/files (admin-only listing with per-file metadata + in-post reference status), DELETE /api/upload/files/{year}/{month}/{filename} (admin-only, refuses deletion of images referenced by any post content or cover_image), a frontend /admin/media page (grid, preview, copy-URL, delete with ref-status), and an insert-from-library picker in the post editor toolbar that inserts the markdown at the cursor. Pure filesystem walk + read-only scan of Post.content/cover_image for /static/uploads/ references — no DB schema change (respects DEC-009 DDL-preserving constraint). Backend verified against dev pg (10.112.9.49:13310, per operator directive); frontend verified via Vitest + build + e2e.
DEC-183.alternatives_rejected: Email/RSS digest subscriptions (needs SMTP infra + a whole deliverability surface, much larger scope); comment reactions / like buttons on comments (relitigated at DEC-059/062, low marginal value); PWA offline shell (rejected repeatedly, no backend involvement); automatic image downscaling/WebP transcoding (would risk the proven upload validation path and needs new deps; a later milestone can add it on top of the library); a DB-backed media table (over-engineered for a filesystem-backed store; reference scan is read-only and cheap at blog scale).

DEC-185.title: Milestone: optimize uploaded images at ingest (smaller storage/page weight, EXIF stripped) — next feature after the media library (DEC-183 deferred it)
DEC-185.rationale: Feature-evolution gap analysis (§11.2) + recorded backlog: DEC-183 explicitly deferred "automatic image downscaling/WebP transcoding" as a later slice on top of the media library (rejected there only as scope, not value). Today upload_image stores bytes verbatim, so a phone-camera 3MB JPEG stays 3MB forever and carries EXIF (often GPS) to every reader — page weight cost and a privacy leak for a blog that serves these images to anonymous visitors. Deliver a pure backend slice: after the existing magic-byte + Pillow-decode validation (kept as step one, unchanged contract), re-encode through Pillow in the SAME format (ext/URL unchanged, so reference-tracking and existing markdown stay valid; zero DDL per DEC-009) with size-optimizing settings (JPEG 85%/optimize/progressive, PNG optimize, WebP method 6; GIF/animated left as-is), and only keep the result if it is actually smaller than the original (never-larger guarantee). EXIF/GPS is dropped by the re-encode (Pillow only preserves it when explicitly passed). Any re-encode failure falls back to the original validated bytes (never reject a valid upload).
DEC-185.alternatives_rejected: Downscale to fixed dimensions/thumbnails (changes intrinsic image data readers may want; the library lists real dimensions so a capped-width compression should not silently destroy resolution — later slice can add responsive sizes on top); transcode everything to WebP (changes extension -> breaks every existing /static/uploads/... reference and markdown; not net-safe); strip EXIF via exifread without re-encode (Pillow re-save already drops it and also shrinks); client-side optimization only (backend ingest covers all clients incl. paste/API).

DEC-190.title: ISS-112 fix: re-bind anonymous push subscriptions on reader sign-in (frontend timing fix, not backend)

DEC-193.title: Close ISS-113: batch the new-post fan-out prune (supersedes DEC-176) — one window-function delete instead of per-reader SELECT+DELETE+commit
DEC-193.rationale: DEC-176 deferred the O(2n) per-reader prune in record_new_post_notifications 'if follower fan-outs grow' — they have (the blog accumulates series/category followers). Follower count is now the multiplier: a heavily followed post pays n SELECTs + n DELETEs + n commits today. Revisit is sanctioned by revisiting the deferred decision. Fix: build every row, one flush + a single set-based window-function prune (ROW_NUMBER partitioned by reader, portable SQLite/Postgres) + one atomic commit. Single-reader paths (reply/thread) keep record_reader_notification unchanged.
DEC-193.alternatives_rejected: Keep per-reader prune (the measured O(2n) cost DEC-176 accepted — now the fan-out multiplier is real); prune only the batch's own rows (wrong — must keep the per-reader cap over the whole inbox, which is what the window function over all rows does); do it with a Python-side grouped sort of all rows then batched not-in delete (window function is a single portable statement, no unbounded IN list).

DEC-194.title: Admin reader management milestone (operator visibility + deactivation of registered readers)
DEC-194.rationale: Feature-evolution gap analysis (§11.2): the reader-accounts arc (DEC-059/062/066/098/106) delivered self-registration, bookmarks, comment history, trust-tier auto-approve and self-service account deletion, but the operator side was never built — registered readers are invisible (no admin list anywhere) and cannot be deactivated. This is now a moderation/security hole: the trust tier (DEC-098) auto-approves any verified reader's comments, so a script-registered account publishes without review and there is no way to stop it — reader_accounts has no is_active flag, get_current_reader validates only existence+token_version, and existing reader JWTs live up to READER_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS. Stakeholder: the blog operator. Acceptance (1 sentence): an admin can list registered readers (email, display name, joined, last login, comment/bookmark counts) with pagination+search and deactivate/reactivate a reader, and a deactivated reader is immediately blocked from sign-in and their existing JWT stops working. Why now: completes the reader-accounts arc with its missing operator counterpart and closes a real spam-approval vector. DEC-195.title: Milestone: reader tag-follow (DEC-195) — a signed-in reader follows a tag and gets a new-post push + inbox row whenever the author publishes a post carrying that tag
DEC-195.rationale: Feature-evolution gap analysis (§11.2): tags are already a first-class subscription axis — DEC-074 scoped RSS/Atom feeds per category/tag, and DEC-076/140 built durable reader-level category follows that fan out new-post push + durable inbox rows (DEC-160) behind one per-kind new_post opt-out (DEC-171). But a reader can only follow categories (coarse: an entire taxonomy) and series (one workflow), never tags (fine-grained topics like 'rust' or 'postgres'). DEC-194 explicitly deferred reader-facing tag-follow as 'real value' with no moderation driver — with the reader-accounts arc closed (DEC-194/CHG-225) and the follow->fan-out->inbox->prefs stack now mature, that deferred value is deliverable. Stakeholder: signed-in readers. Acceptance (1 sentence): a signed-in reader follows a tag from the public tag surface and thereafter receives a new-post push + inbox row when the author publishes a post carrying that tag (honoring the DEC-171 new_post opt-out), with follows manageable from the account page. Why now: categories are too coarse for topic alerting on a multi-topic blog and scoped RSS feeds (DEC-074) sit outside the app; tag-follow is the only reader-facing follow dimension the taxonomy lacks. Additive scope: a new tag_follows table (reader_id, tag_id, notify, UNIQUE reader+tag) with no existing DDL touched (DEC-009); follower fan-out joins the published post's tags in both crud.record_new_post_notifications and webpush.dispatch_new_post; new reader endpoints /api/reader/me/tags/{tag_id}/follow (PUT/PATCH/DELETE) + list; follows-feed union joins tags; frontend follow + notify control on the tag surface and a Followed-tags section on the account page.
DEC-195.alternatives_rejected: Category-only follow is enough (categories are coarse — a reader wanting 'new posts about rust' on a multi-topic blog gets flooded by unrelated posts; tags exist precisely as the finer axis, DEC-074 already scope feeds per tag); pure pull: rely on the tag-scoped RSS/Atom feed (DEC-074) instead (feeds sit outside the app; the gap is push + in-app inbox, not feed availability); tag bundles / multi-tag topic groups (over-engineering for a personal blog — single-tag follow with per-tag notify control covers the need); reader-view analytics/impressions page (observability only, no reader-facing value — still deferred).

DEC-197.title: Milestone: email notification channel (DEC-197) — a per-kind opt-in email copy of the reader notification fan-out, closing the last delivery gap in the follow/notification arc
DEC-197.rationale: Feature-evolution sourcing (§11.2 gap analysis): the follow/notification stack is otherwise complete — durable inbox (DEC-160), browser push with per-kind opt-outs (DEC-171), unread badge + mark-read, per-follow notify toggles, and now tag-follow (DEC-195/196). But every delivery channel requires the site to be open (in-app inbox) or the browser to have push permission and run (Web Push). Email is the only medium that reaches a reader who never re-opens the blog — the single biggest retention hole left in the arc, and the one channel mainstream blog platforms all have. Stakeholder: signed-in readers (opt-in per kind) + the operator (recovers off-site readers). Acceptance (1 sentence): a reader who enables email for a kind receives a plain-text + HTML email to their registered address when that event fires (new post in a followed series/category/tag, a reply to their comment, a comment on a followed thread), the notifications prefs page exposes an email channel per kind (off by default), delivery is best-effort over the configured SMTP host, and tests assert the outbound message via a captured SMTP session. Why now: the arc is complete except this channel; additive and purely opt-in, so existing push/inbox behavior is untouched. Scope: three additive email_* columns on reader_notification_prefs (off by default; DEC-009 additive DDL), a new app/emailer.py (smtplib + STARTTLS, HTML+text, escaping, best-effort), wiring at the three existing dispatch points (crud.record_new_post_notifications for new_post/series_new_part; comments._notify_thread_subscribers; comments._notify_replied_to) gated on ReaderAccount.email + the reader email prefs, prefs API/schema growth (6 kinds incl. email_*), notifications-page email toggles + en/zh, backend tests (prefs API, fan-out gating, emailer with a captured SMTP), frontend component tests, and an e2e journey against an SMTP sink.
DEC-197.alternatives_rejected: Skip email entirely (retention stays limited to site-open push/inbox — readers who never return miss everything, the arc is then half-finished vs mainstream platforms); a weekly newsletter/digest instead of per-event email (aggregation + scheduling is a much bigger slice and can be layered on the same fan-out later; per-event email is the foundation); email for anonymous commenters too (their free-text email is untrusted PII and not stored — DEC-160 comment, email stays reader-only); email default-on for everyone (spammy and GDPR-hostile — email must be a per-kind opt-in); a reply-by-email inbound workflow (needs inbound SMTP parsing — way out of scope for this slice).

DEC-201.title: Milestone: weekly email digest (recurring content discovery for opted-in readers)
DEC-201.rationale: Build on the delivered per-event email channel (DEC-197/198): a signed-in reader who opts into the weekly digest gets one HTML email per week listing public posts newly published since their last digest (7-day window cap). User story: a casual reader who follows few categories misses most posts and does not want per-event mail; the digest is the re-engagement/periodic-discovery surface every personal blog needs. Why now: DEC-199 named this as the remaining differentiated capability vs. the patch-increment candidates; the emailer + prefs plumbing is healthy, and the operator directed a new milestone. Delivery: backend job + CLI + admin send-now endpoint, per-reader opt-in pref (off by default) + digest_sent_at idempotency, PG advisory lock guard for multi-worker cron, HTML template with absolute links + unsubscribe. Vertical slice with unit/integration/e2e + real-Postgres smoke.
DEC-201.alternatives_rejected: Not a follow-scoped digest (digest is site-wide discovery; per-event email already covers follows; scoped digest a possible later option); not a daily digest (noise; weekly is the newsletter default); not an in-process APScheduler timer (multi-worker double-send + no persistence; prefer external cron via CLI + manual admin button with advisory-lock guard); not relying on push/inbox alone (misses off-site readers - the gap the email channel closes); not the test-email button or PostCard-chip links (rejected patch increments in DEC-199)

ISS-124.title: Nav unread-notification badge desyncs from the /notifications inbox
ISS-124.description: default.vue refreshUnread() runs exactly once on mount (the comment says 'polled' but there is no interval), and the /notifications page tracks its own local unread ref. Marking notifications read on /notifications (markRead/markAllRead) or signing in later never updates the nav badge; only a full page reload shows the correct count. A signed-in reader sees a stale badge (or a permanently-hidden badge) until reload.

TASK-224.title: Share the unread-notification badge state between layout and /notifications (ISS-124)
TASK-224.description: Add a module-level useNotificationBadge() composable (unreadCount ref + refresh + visibility-aware 60s polling, same singleton pattern as useReaderAuth). default.vue consumes it (replacing its one-shot local refreshUnread, wiring watch(isAuthenticated) so login starts / logout stops polling). /notifications.vue calls refresh() after load/markRead/markAllRead so the nav badge drops immediately. Unit test for the composable.

TASK-225.title: Desktop nav overflows/clips at xl widths (English + signed-in reader)
TASK-225.description: ISS-125: the desktop nav (breakpoint moved md->xl) shows all 11 links + search + push + auth + lang + theme. With English locale and a signed-in reader the row overflows the xl (1280px) viewport; the original justify-end + overflow-x-auto combination clips left-most links (flex-end overflow goes to the flex-start side, scrollLeft cannot go negative, scrollWidth stays == clientWidth — CSS probe confirmed FIRST never visible). Fix: right-align via first:ml-auto on the first link (NOT justify-end) so overflowing rows scroll from the start (verified in Chromium at 1280px: all links reachable; at 1600px: right-aligned unchanged). HeaderSearch narrowed w-56->w-44; SubscribeButton gained a compact prop: header nav renders it compact (label hidden below 2xl), mobile menu keeps full text (unconditional 2xl-hiding would have left the <xl-only menu icon-only forever).

ISS-125.title: Desktop nav clips the left-most links at xl viewport widths once a reader is signed in (English)
ISS-125.description: The desktop nav lives at xl+ (1280px). In English with the reader signed in (11 links + search + subscribe + sign-out + lang + theme), the row overflows at 1280-~1500px. The header used justify-end + overflow-x-auto, which clips the left-most items: flex-end alignment pushes overflow to the main-start side, scrollLeft() cannot go negative, and scrollWidth stays equal to clientWidth, so the browser reports no scrollable overflow and the first links are unreachable — directly contradicting the 'no nav item is ever unreachable' invariant. CSS probe in real Chromium confirmed FIRST (left-most link) never becomes visible under justify-end. Fix switched to margin-left:auto on the first link (collapses when over capacity → row scrolls from start).

CHG-247.summary: Shared nav unread-badge state via useNotificationBadge() (module-level singleton mirroring useReaderAuth): default.vue drives visibility-aware 60s polling from watch(isAuthenticated)/onMounted/onUnmounted; /notifications re-fetches the shared count from the server after load/markRead/markAllRead (server truth, never overwrites a fresher poll value). Also fixes two desktop-nav usability regressions: (1) links+search group now right-aligns via first:ml-auto instead of justify-end, which had clipped left-most links on signed-in English overflow (flex-end+overflow hides main-start side; auto margin collapses to 0 so the row scrolls from start — verified in Chromium); (2) chrome controls (push/account/language/theme) moved outside the scroll container as fixed siblings so they stay reachable even where a vertical wheel doesn't pan overflow-x (Firefox); SubscribeButton gained a compact prop (header icon-only below 2xl, mobile menu keeps full label). Reflects a code review that verified the CSS claim correct and cleared the change with notes (2 MEDIUM + 2 LOW, all addressed: stale-badge overwrite, Firefox right-edge reachability, test-order coupling, logout race).

EV-205.description: code-reviewer agent reviewed the WIP (50/50 affected tests pass on review). Verdict: APPROVE with notes, no CRITICAL/HIGH. Findings and resolution: (1) MEDIUM — justify-end+hidden-scrollbar could strand right-edge controls at 1280-1400px in Firefox (no vertical-wheel→overflow-x panning): fixed by splitting chrome controls (push/account/language/theme) out of the scroll container as fixed siblings — verified visible at 1280/1440/1680 in Chromium.
